intent.raw_query: Seoul K-culture and food, $2200 couple, winter 2026 from LAX

experiences.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Rental
experiences.description: Explore the grand Joseon-era Gyeongbokgung Palace while dressed in a traditional Hanbok rented from nearby shops. Stroll through the palace grounds, watch the royal guard-changing ceremony, and take stunning photos at one of Seoul's most iconic landmarks. Many rental shops offer free entry to the palace with Hanbok rental.

experiences.name: Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive deep into Seoul's legendary street food scene at Gwangjang Market, one of Korea's oldest and largest traditional markets. Sample iconic dishes like bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap (addictive mini rice rolls), tteokbokki, and fresh yukhoe (beef tartare) straight from the stalls. A true sensory feast beloved by locals and food lovers alike.

experiences.name: K-Pop Idol Experience & SMTOWN Museum
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the heart of K-pop culture at SMTOWN COEX Artium, an interactive museum and entertainment complex dedicated to SM Entertainment's biggest artists including EXO, aespa, and SHINee. Enjoy hologram performances, photo zones, artist exhibitions, and browse exclusive merchandise. Afterward, explore the surrounding COEX Mall for more K-culture shopping.

experiences.name: Bukchon Hanok Village & Insadong Cultural Walk
experiences.description: Wander through the beautifully preserved Bukchon Hanok Village, where hundreds of traditional Korean hanok houses line narrow hillside alleys with breathtaking views of the city. Then stroll down to the charming Insadong district to browse traditional tea houses, Korean craft shops, and art galleries. End with a cup of traditional omija tea at a historic teahouse.

experiences.name: Korean Cooking Class & Han River Picnic
experiences.description: Join a hands-on Korean cooking class in Mapo-gu to learn how to make classic dishes like bibimbap, japchae, and kimchi from a local chef. Afterward, pack your creations and head to the scenic Han River Park for a classic Korean-style picnic — a beloved local pastime. Rent a bike along the riverside path to complete the authentic Seoul local experience.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Seoul, South Korea
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Incheon International Airport at 13:00. Take the AREX (Airport Railroad Express) to Hongik University Station, then transfer to Line 3 toward Gyeongbokgung Station (approx. 70-80 min, ~₩4,750). Check in to Boutique Stay in Gyeongbokgung, Jongno-gu. Drop luggage and freshen up. Take a short orientation walk around the Gyeongbokgung Palace walls and Gwanghwamun Square to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Insadong-gil (10-min walk from hotel) — browse traditional crafts, street snacks, and indie shops. Explore the charming Ssamziegil courtyard complex for free. Enjoy the festive December street atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: N/A (in-flight or airport snack)
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at Incheon Airport food court — try Bibimbap or Kimbap for around ₩8,000–₩10,000
meals.dinner: Insadong Myeonok or a local pojangmacha (street food tent) near Insadong — try Tteokbokki, Hotteok (sweet pancake), and Odeng (fish cake skewers) for ₩5,000–₩8,000 total

day_by_day.notes: Get a T-money card at the airport or any convenience store (CU, GS25, 7-Eleven) for ₩3,000 and load it with ₩30,000–₩50,000 for subway/bus travel. December is cold (0°C to -5°C), so dress in warm layers. Carry hand warmers.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gyeongbokgung Palace (5-min walk from hotel). Arrive by 10:00 to catch the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony at the Heungnyemun Gate (10:00 & 14:00). Entrance fee: ₩3,000. Explore the palace grounds, Gyeonghoeru Pavilion, and the National Folk Museum of Korea (free entry within palace grounds).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk north to Bukchon Hanok Village (15-min walk) — wander the scenic alleyways lined with traditional hanok houses. Free to explore. Then head to Changdeokgung Palace & the Secret Garden (Huwon) — entry ₩3,000 for palace, ₩5,000 for guided Secret Garden tour (book in advance online).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Gwanghwamun Square for the winter light festival decorations. Walk to Cheonggyecheon Stream (20-min walk or 1 subway stop) for a peaceful evening stroll along the illuminated waterway — free. Return to Insadong area for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast (GS25 or CU near hotel) — triangle kimbap, instant ramen cup, banana milk for ₩3,000–₩4,000
meals.lunch: Tosokchon Samgyetang (near Gyeongbokgung) — famous ginseng chicken soup for ₩17,000 (a splurge worth it for the cultural experience)
meals.dinner: Insadong area — Juk (Korean porridge) at Bon Juk or a local Korean set meal (백반, Baekban) for ₩7,000–₩9,000

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays, so Wednesday is perfect. Wear comfortable walking shoes — you'll cover 8–10 km today. The Secret Garden tour requires advance booking; check the official website.

day_by_day.morning: Take Line 3 to Anguk Station and visit Jogyesa Temple (free entry) — the main Buddhist temple in Seoul, beautifully decorated in December. Then walk to the nearby Unhyeongung Palace (₩1,000 entry) for a quieter, less-touristy royal residence experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the subway to Dongdaemun (Line 4 or 5, ~20 min). Explore Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — free exterior and select indoor exhibitions. Browse Gwangjang Market (5-min walk from DDP) for a vibrant traditional market experience — one of Seoul's oldest markets.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Gwangjang Market for dinner — it's a street food paradise. Then walk or take a short bus ride to Dongdaemun shopping district for evening window shopping. Return to hotel by subway.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or a local bakery near hotel — Paris Baguette or Tous Les Jours for ₩3,000–₩5,000
meals.lunch: Gwangjang Market street food — Bindaetteok (mung bean pancake ₩4,000), Mayak Kimbap (₩3,000), Yukhoe (beef tartare ₩10,000) — budget ₩10,000–₩15,000 total
meals.dinner: Gwangjang Market food stalls — more street food exploration or a sit-down stall for Japchae or Bibimbap for ₩8,000–₩12,000

day_by_day.notes: Gwangjang Market is one of the most authentic food markets in Seoul — don't miss Bindaetteok and Mayak Kimbap. DDP hosts various free exhibitions; check their schedule online. Dongdaemun area comes alive at night.

day_by_day.morning: Take Line 2 to Hongdae (Hongik University) Station (~30 min). Explore the vibrant Hongdae street art, murals, and indie culture scene. Visit the Free Market area (weekends are busier, but the neighborhood is lively daily). Browse unique vintage and K-fashion shops along Hongdae main streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short bus to nearby Sinchon — explore the youthful commercial street popular with university students. Then head to Yonsei University campus for a free scenic walk (beautiful even in winter). Return to Hongdae area to explore more cafes and K-pop merchandise stores.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Hongdae nightlife — street busking performances (especially on weekends), live music at small indie clubs, or a norebang (karaoke) session at a budget karaoke room (₩10,000–₩15,000/hour). Return to hotel by subway.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area convenience store or local cafe near Gyeongbokgung
meals.lunch: Hongdae area — try a Korean BBQ lunch set at a local restaurant for ₩10,000–₩13,000, or Tteokbokki + Sundae combo at a bunsik restaurant for ₩7,000
meals.dinner: Hongdae street food or a local Chimaek (chicken + beer) restaurant — budget ₩12,000–₩18,000 including a drink

day_by_day.notes: Hongdae is the hub of K-culture, indie music, and youth fashion. Look for SM, YG, or HYBE merchandise stores nearby. Friday evenings are lively with street performers. The area has many affordable cafes perfect for K-culture immersion.

day_by_day.morning: Take Line 6 to Mapo-gu area and visit Mangwon Market (망원시장) — a local neighborhood market less touristy than Namdaemun, beloved by locals. Browse fresh produce, street food, and everyday Korean life. Then stroll along the nearby Hangang River park (Mangwon Hangang Park) for winter river views — free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the subway to Itaewon (Line 6, ~15 min). Explore the multicultural Itaewon district — browse Antique Furniture Street, Haebangchon (HBC) neighborhood, and the eclectic mix of shops. Visit Leeum Samsung Museum of Art if budget allows (₩10,000–₩20,000) or enjoy the free exterior architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Namsan Seoul Tower via bus or cable car from Myeongdong (₩9,000 round trip cable car). View the city lights from N Seoul Tower observation deck (₩16,000) or enjoy the free view from the Namsan Park hilltop. Attach a love lock if you wish (locks sold nearby).

meals.breakfast: Mangwon Market — fresh Hotteok, Gyeranppang (egg bread ₩1,500), and Tteokbokki for under ₩5,000
meals.lunch: Itaewon — try a local Korean diner or a budget Shawarma/international option for ₩8,000–₩12,000
meals.dinner: Myeongdong street food before Namsan — Lobster Gratin skewer, Cheese Corn Dog, Tornado Potato for ₩8,000–₩12,000 total

day_by_day.notes: Namsan Tower is magical in December with winter lights. Dress very warmly — it's significantly colder at the top of Namsan hill. The free hilltop viewpoint is nearly as good as the paid tower deck. Myeongdong is extremely lively on Saturday evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Namdaemun Market (남대문시장) — one of Korea's largest traditional markets, open since the 15th century. Explore the ginseng section, clothing stalls, kitchenware, and street food alleys. Then walk 10 min to Myeongdong shopping district for K-beauty product browsing (many free samples!).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take Line 4 to Dongdaemun History & Culture Park and visit the Dongdaemun Gate (Heunginjimun) — free to photograph. Explore the surrounding Dongdaemun fashion wholesale district. Then head to Cheonggyecheon Stream for a daytime walk — the stream runs 5.8 km and is free.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Myeongdong for Sunday evening street food market — one of Seoul's best street food experiences. Then explore명동 (Myeongdong) main street for K-pop stores, cosmetics, and lively atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Namdaemun Market — Galchi Jorim (braised fish) or Kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup) at a market restaurant for ₩6,000–₩8,000
meals.lunch: Myeongdong area — Myeongdong Kyoja (famous handmade noodles, ₩10,000–₩12,000) — one of Seoul's most iconic budget restaurants
meals.dinner: Myeongdong street food stalls — Corn dogs, Tteokbokki, Haemul Pajeon (seafood pancake), and more for ₩10,000–₩15,000

day_by_day.notes: Myeongdong Kyoja often has queues — arrive by 11:30 for lunch to avoid the longest wait. Namdaemun Market is best in the morning. K-beauty shops in Myeongdong give generous free samples — great way to try products without spending. Sunday markets are vibrant.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress (수원화성) — take subway Line 1 from Jonggak Station to Suwon Station (~1 hour, ₩2,500). Walk to Hwaseong Fortress (15 min from station or bus). Entrance: ₩1,000. Walk the 5.7 km fortress wall for panoramic views — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Visit Hwaseong Haenggung Palace (₩1,500).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Suwon's Paldalmun Gate area and the traditional Suwon Jidong Market near the fortress. Browse local stalls and soak in the historical atmosphere. Begin heading back to Seoul by 15:00.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul (arrive ~16:30). Head to Gwanghwamun area for a relaxed evening walk. Visit a traditional Korean tea house (Insadong area) for warm Yujacha (citron tea) or Sikhye (rice punch) — perfect for a cold December evening.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store near hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Suwon Galbi (Suwon-style short ribs) — Suwon is famous for this dish. Try at a local restaurant near the fortress for ₩12,000–₩18,000, or cheaper pork ribs option for ₩10,000
meals.dinner: Insadong traditional tea house meal or a local Korean restaurant near hotel for ₩8,000–₩10,000

day_by_day.notes: Start early (by 9:00) to maximize time at Hwaseong Fortress. The fortress walk takes 2–3 hours at a relaxed pace. Suwon Galbi is a must-try local specialty — look for restaurants along Haenggung-ro. Bring a portable charger as you'll be away from the hotel all day.

day_by_day.morning: Take Line 2 to Gangnam Station. Explore the upscale Gangnam district — window shop along Garosu-gil (tree-lined street with boutiques and cafes, free to stroll). Visit the free COEX Starfield Library inside COEX Mall — a stunning Instagram-worthy library with thousands of books (free entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore COEX Mall and the adjacent Bongeunsa Temple (봉은사) — a serene Buddhist temple in the heart of Gangnam (free entry, donations welcome). Contrast the ancient temple with the modern skyscrapers around it. Take the subway to Apgujeong Rodeo Street for K-fashion and K-beauty browsing.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Banpo Bridge area (short taxi or bus from Gangnam) for the Moonlight Rainbow Fountain show — check seasonal schedule as it may not run in winter. If unavailable, enjoy a Han River night view from Banpo Hangang Park (free). Return to hotel.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery or convenience store near hotel
meals.lunch: Gangnam area — try a Korean lunch special (점심 특선) at a local restaurant for ₩8,000–₩12,000, or food court in COEX Mall for ₩9,000–₩13,000
meals.dinner: Gangnam-gu local restaurant — Sundubu Jjigae (soft tofu stew) set meal for ₩9,000–₩11,000

day_by_day.notes: COEX Starfield Library is free but photography for social media is popular — visit on a weekday morning to avoid crowds. Bongeunsa Temple is one of the most atmospheric temples in Seoul, especially in the evening with lanterns. Gangnam is pricier but window shopping is free.

day_by_day.morning: Take Line 3 or 6 to Yongsan and visit the War Memorial of Korea (전쟁기념관) — free entry, one of the best museums in Seoul covering Korean history, the Korean War, and military heritage. Outdoor exhibits include tanks, aircraft, and warships. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Itaewon for a revisit or explore the Haebangchon (HBC) neighborhood — a quirky, artsy hillside community with murals, indie cafes, and international restaurants. Then take the subway to Gyeongui-Jungang Line to Seongsu Station — explore Seongsu-dong (Seoul's Brooklyn), known for its converted factory cafes and artisan workshops.
day_by_day.evening: Seongsu-dong evening — explore the trendy cafes and small galleries. Visit the Under Stand Avenue (언더스탠드 에비뉴) — a creative cultural space made from shipping containers with shops and food. Return to hotel by subway.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area or convenience store
meals.lunch: War Memorial area — packed lunch from convenience store or nearby Kimbap restaurant for ₩5,000–₩7,000
meals.dinner: Seongsu-dong — try a local cafe-restaurant or a trendy but affordable eatery. Seongsu has great Sourdough bakeries and fusion Korean food for ₩10,000–₩15,000

day_by_day.notes: The War Memorial of Korea is genuinely excellent and completely free — don't skip it. Seongsu-dong is Seoul's most Instagram-worthy neighborhood and is very popular with young Koreans. December evenings in Seongsu are atmospheric with warm cafe lights.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changgyeonggung Palace (창경궁) — one of the less-visited royal palaces, quieter and more intimate than Gyeongbokgung (₩1,000 entry). Connected to Jongmyo Shrine (유네스코 세계문화유산) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the royal ancestral shrine (₩1,000 entry). Allow 2–3 hours for both.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Naksan Park (낙산공원) via the Seoul City Wall trail — free, scenic views of the city from the old fortress wall. The walk from Hyehwa Station takes ~30 min uphill. Visit Ihwa Mural Village (이화 벽화마을) — a charming hillside neighborhood covered in murals, including the famous Moon Cat mural.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve in Seoul! Head to Myeongdong — the area transforms beautifully for Christmas with lights and decorations. Attend a Christmas Eve mass at Myeongdong Cathedral (명동성당) if interested — one of Korea's most iconic Catholic churches, free. Enjoy the festive street food and atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery — Christmas-themed pastries are everywhere in Seoul in late December
meals.lunch: Hyehwa area near Naksan Park — try a local Kalguksu (knife-cut noodle soup) restaurant for ₩8,000–₩10,000
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve special — treat yourself slightly: Myeongdong area Korean BBQ (삼겹살, pork belly) at a local grill restaurant for ₩12,000–₩18,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve is one of the most festive nights in Seoul — Koreans celebrate it as a romantic holiday. Myeongdong Cathedral's Christmas Eve service is atmospheric and open to all. Book dinner early if dining at a restaurant as many places fill up. The city lights are spectacular.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Day — visit Jogyesa Temple for morning Buddhist atmosphere (free). Then head to Gyeongbokgung Palace for another visit — try wearing a Hanbok (traditional Korean clothing) rental from one of the many shops near the palace (₩15,000–₩20,000 for 2 hours). Hanbok wearers get free palace entry!
day_by_day.afternoon: Take Line 3 to Gyeongbokgung and walk to the National Museum of Korea (국립중앙박물관) — take Line 4 to Ichon Station. One of the largest museums in Asia with 13,000+ artifacts — completely FREE. Allow 2–3 hours. Explore Korean history from prehistoric times through the Joseon Dynasty.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Lotte World Tower area (잠실) — the 555m tower is lit up spectacularly for Christmas. Enjoy the exterior light show and the Seokchon Lake Christmas decorations (free). Browse Lotte World Mall food court for dinner. Return to hotel.

meals.breakfast: Christmas morning — splurge slightly on a cafe breakfast near Gyeongbokgung for ₩7,000–₩10,000
meals.lunch: National Museum of Korea cafeteria — affordable Korean set meals for ₩8,000–₩12,000
meals.dinner: Lotte World Mall food court — Korean food options for ₩9,000–₩13,000, or street food around Seokchon Lake

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum of Korea is one of Seoul's absolute must-visits and is completely free — remarkable value. Hanbok rental near Gyeongbokgung is a quintessential K-culture experience and gets you free palace entry. Seokchon Lake Christmas lights are among Seoul's most beautiful winter displays.

day_by_day.morning: Take Line 4 to Seoul Station and explore the Seoul Station Old Building (문화역서울 284) — a beautifully restored 1925 Renaissance-style building now used as a cultural arts center, free entry. Then walk to Namdaemun Market again for any last-minute souvenir shopping (great prices on Korean snacks, ginseng, dried seaweed, and traditional crafts).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the cable car or hike up to Inwangsan Mountain (인왕산) — accessible from Dongnimmun Station (Line 3). A relatively easy hike with spectacular views of Seoul and the city wall. Free. The Shamanist Guksadang shrine near the top is a unique cultural experience. Allow 2–3 hours for the hike.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Insadong — browse the last-minute souvenir shops (traditional tea, Korean snacks, hanji paper goods). Enjoy a final walk through Bukchon or along Cheonggyecheon Stream. Treat yourself to a final Korean BBQ dinner or a traditional Korean feast.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store near hotel or local kimbap restaurant
meals.lunch: Namdaemun Market — market food stalls for ₩6,000–₩9,000
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner — Insadong area traditional Korean restaurant. Try a full Hanjeongsik (Korean table d'hôte) if budget allows (₩15,000–₩25,000) or a classic Doenjang Jjigae (soybean paste stew) set for ₩9,000

day_by_day.notes: Inwangsan is best hiked in the morning or early afternoon — it gets dark early in December (around 17:30). Wear sturdy shoes and warm layers. The mountain is considered sacred by Korean Shamanism practitioners. Namdaemun Market is excellent for budget souvenirs — negotiate prices at clothing stalls.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Seoul. Depending on departure time, take a last walk around Gyeongbokgung Palace walls and Gwanghwamun Square. Visit a nearby jjimjilbang (Korean sauna/bathhouse) for a relaxing final morning experience — budget ₩10,000–₩15,000 for entry. Bukcheon Jjimjilbang or a local one near the hotel. Pack bags and check out.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the airport via AREX from Seoul Station or Hongik University Station. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for travel time and airport check-in. Pick up last-minute snacks and gifts at the airport duty-free or convenience stores (Lotte Mart in airport is great for Korean snacks at good prices).
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final Korean breakfast — a local restaurant near hotel for Haejang-guk (hangover soup/hearty soup) or Gyeran Mari (rolled omelette) with rice for ₩7,000–₩9,000
meals.lunch: Airport food court or convenience store — grab Korean snacks and a light meal before departure
meals.dinner: In-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: AREX to Incheon Airport from Seoul Station takes ~43 minutes (₩9,500 direct express) or ~66 minutes on the all-stop train (₩4,750). Check your flight time carefully and plan departure from hotel accordingly. Many hotels offer luggage storage if you check out early. The airport has a Korean Cultural Street on the 3rd floor — worth a final browse.

trip_options.title: Classic Seoul, South Korea Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Incheon International Airport at 13:00 — clear customs, collect luggage, and take the AREX Express Train (~43 min) to Seoul Station, then transfer to Gyeongbokgung area. Check in to the boutique stay and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a gentle orientation walk around the immediate Gyeongbokgung neighborhood. Stroll along Gyeongbokgung Palace's outer walls and explore the charming Bukchon Hanok Village entrance area to get your bearings. Browse nearby local shops selling Korean crafts and souvenirs on Insadong-gil.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Insadong Street for a relaxed first evening. Explore the Ssamziegil courtyard complex — a multi-level indie shopping and cultural space — and enjoy the festive December atmosphere with seasonal lights.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at Seoul Station food court — try Kimbap or a warm bowl of Tteokguk (rice cake soup) for around ₩7,000–10,000
meals.dinner: Tosokchon Samgyetang (토속촌 삼계탕) near Gyeongbokgung — famous whole chicken ginseng soup, a comforting classic after a long flight. ~₩18,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Jet lag may be a factor. Hydrate well and sleep early to reset your body clock. December in Seoul is cold (0–5°C), so layer up immediately after landing.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gyeongbokgung Palace right at opening (9:00 AM) — it's steps from your hotel. Watch the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony at the main gate (Gwanghwamun) at 10:00 AM. Explore the grand palace grounds including Geunjeongjeon throne hall and Gyeonghoeru Pavilion. Consider renting a Hanbok at the palace entrance for free admission and beautiful winter photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk north to the National Folk Museum of Korea located within the palace grounds (included with palace ticket). Explore exhibitions on traditional Korean daily life, seasonal customs, and folk culture. Afterward, walk to Bukchon Hanok Village for a self-guided tour through the preserved traditional Korean houses.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Samcheong-dong neighborhood — lined with independent galleries, cafes, and boutique shops. Browse contemporary Korean art at small galleries along the main street.

meals.breakfast: Cafe near the hotel — try a Korean-style breakfast of Doenjang Jjigae (soybean paste stew) and rice at a local restaurant. ~₩8,000
meals.lunch: Gwangjang Market-style packed lunch box from a nearby stall, or dine at a local Jongno-gu restaurant serving Bibimbap. ~₩10,000
meals.dinner: Samcheong-dong Sujebi (삼청동 수제비) — handmade dough soup restaurant, a beloved local spot. ~₩12,000

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung Palace opens at 9:00 AM and is closed on Tuesdays. December lighting makes the palace especially atmospheric. Wear warm shoes — cobblestones can be icy.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace and its famous Secret Garden (Huwon). Book the Secret Garden guided tour in advance online (~₩8,000 extra). The winter garden with bare trees and frozen ponds has a hauntingly beautiful aesthetic. The palace itself is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Changgyeonggung Palace next door (combo ticket available) and then cross into Jongmyo Shrine — the royal ancestral shrine, also a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The serene, minimalist architecture is profoundly moving in winter silence.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) via subway (Dongdaemun History & Culture Park station). Marvel at the futuristic Zaha Hadid-designed building illuminated at night. Browse the surrounding Dongdaemun shopping district and night markets.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area bakery — Paris Baguette or a local Korean bakery for pastries and coffee. ~₩6,000
meals.lunch: Ikseon-dong Hanok Village alley restaurants — try a warm bowl of Galbitang (beef short rib soup) at a traditional house-turned-restaurant. ~₩15,000
meals.dinner: Dongdaemun area — Mayfield Pojangmacha (street food tent) for Tteokbokki, Eomuk (fish cake skewers), and Hotteok (sweet pancakes). ~₩10,000

day_by_day.notes: Changdeokgung Secret Garden tours are limited in number — book at the official palace website ahead of time. Jongmyo Shrine is closed on Tuesdays. DDP has free outdoor areas open late.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Itaewon and walk up to Namsan Mountain. Ride the Namsan Cable Car up (₩15,000 round trip) and visit N Seoul Tower. Enjoy panoramic 360° views of Seoul in the crisp winter air. Add a love lock to the famous fence and explore the observation deck.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend Namsan and explore the surrounding Namsangol Hanok Village at the base — a reconstructed traditional village with free entry. In winter, they often have cultural demonstrations and seasonal events. Then walk or take the subway to Myeongdong for afternoon shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Spend the evening in Myeongdong — one of Seoul's most vibrant commercial districts. Explore the outdoor street food stalls (especially lively on Friday evenings), browse Korean cosmetics flagship stores (Innisfree, Etude House, Sulwhasoo), and experience the electric K-culture atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area — Korean-style breakfast at a local diner: rice, soup, and banchan (side dishes). ~₩9,000
meals.lunch: Namsan area cafe with mountain views, or packed kimbap rolls from a convenience store (GS25/CU) eaten with the view. ~₩5,000
meals.dinner: Myeongdong Kyoja (명동교자) — legendary hand-made noodles and dumplings, a Seoul institution. Expect a short queue. ~₩12,000

day_by_day.notes: N Seoul Tower is especially beautiful at dusk — time your cable car ride for around 4:30 PM to catch sunset and then city lights. Myeongdong on Friday evening is very busy — keep belongings secure.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gwangjang Market (광장시장) — one of Seoul's oldest and most authentic traditional markets. Explore the fabric and clothing sections before the crowds, then dive into the famous food alley. Watch grandmothers hand-making Bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes) and Mayak Kimbap (tiny rice rolls).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along Cheonggyecheon Stream — a beautifully restored urban stream cutting through central Seoul. December often brings the Cheonggyecheon Lantern Festival installations. Walk the 5.8 km stream path or take a section toward City Hall Plaza, which hosts winter ice skating and seasonal events.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Gwanghwamun Square and the surrounding Jongno area after dark. Visit the beautifully lit Cheong Wa Dae (former Blue House presidential residence) area, now open to the public. Stroll back to the hotel through the illuminated Gyeongbokgung palace walls.

meals.breakfast: Gwangjang Market — Mayak Kimbap and a bowl of Yukgaejang (spicy beef soup) for an authentic market breakfast. ~₩8,000
meals.lunch: Cheonggyecheon area — find a local Dosirak (lunch box) restaurant for a budget-friendly set meal with rice, protein, and banchan. ~₩10,000
meals.dinner: Jongno 3-ga area Gopchang (곱창) alley — grilled beef intestines with soju, a true local Friday-night experience. ~₩20,000 including drinks

day_by_day.notes: Gwangjang Market is most atmospheric in the morning. Saturday is the busiest day — arrive at the food alley before 10 AM to avoid long waits. City Hall ice skating rink is popular in December.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the outskirts: Take the subway to Bukhansan National Park (Gupabal or Dobongsan entrance). Enjoy a winter mountain hike through pine forests and granite peaks. The Bukhansanseong Fortress Trail is manageable and offers stunning views of Seoul below.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and head to Seochon Village (서촌) — the neighborhood just west of Gyeongbokgung, often overlooked by tourists. Wander narrow alleys lined with independent cafes, bookshops, and art studios. Visit Tong-in Market for a unique experience: buy old Korean coins and use them to buy traditional snacks from vendors.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed Sunday evening in the Gyeongbokgung/Seochon area. Visit a traditional Korean tea house (Dawon or Cha Masineun Ddeul) for a warm pot of omija (five-flavor berry) tea and traditional rice cakes.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store near the hotel or subway station — triangle kimbap, instant ramyeon cup, and banana milk. ~₩4,000
meals.lunch: Mountain trail packed lunch — buy Gimbap rolls and snacks from a convenience store near the trailhead. ~₩6,000
meals.dinner: Seochon neighborhood — Onggijeong (옹기정) or similar local restaurant for Doenjang Jjigae set meal. ~₩12,000

day_by_day.notes: Bukhansan trails can be icy in December — bring hiking poles or rent them at the entrance. Wear proper hiking boots. The Seochon neighborhood is quieter on Sunday evenings — perfect for a peaceful wind-down.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to K-culture: Visit the HYBE Insight Museum in Yongsan (BTS and K-pop focused interactive museum). Book tickets in advance online (~₩22,000). The immersive exhibitions cover K-pop history, music production, and artist stories.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stay in the Yongsan area and visit the War Memorial of Korea (free entry) — a sobering and comprehensive museum covering Korean military history, the Korean War, and national defense. The outdoor exhibits include tanks, aircraft, and artillery.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Hongdae (Hongik University area) for the evening — Seoul's youth culture epicenter. Experience live busking performances on the main street, browse vinyl record shops and indie clothing stores, and soak in the creative, energetic atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area — try a local Haejang-guk (hangover soup) restaurant for a hearty morning bowl. ~₩10,000
meals.lunch: Yongsan area — Lotte Mart food court in the Yongsan iPark Mall for affordable Korean set meals. ~₩9,000
meals.dinner: Hongdae — Bossam (보쌈) restaurant for boiled pork belly wrapped in napa cabbage with fermented kimchi and shrimp paste. ~₩18,000

day_by_day.notes: HYBE Insight tickets sell out quickly — book at least a week in advance. Monday is a good day to visit War Memorial as weekday crowds are lighter. Hongdae busking is best after 7 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan — one of Asia's largest museums with an extraordinary collection of Korean artifacts from prehistoric times through the Joseon Dynasty. Free general admission. Allow 2–3 hours for highlights including the iconic Gilt-bronze Maitreya Bodhisattva statue.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the Han River to explore Yeouido — Seoul's financial and media island. Walk along the Yeouido Hangang Park riverside (beautiful even in winter). Visit the KBS (Korea Broadcasting System) building area and the nearby Yeouido IFC Mall for some indoor warmth and browsing.
day_by_day.evening: Take the subway to Gangnam for the evening. Walk the famous Gangnam-daero boulevard, visit COEX Mall (Asia's largest underground shopping mall), and browse the Starfield Library inside COEX — a stunning floor-to-ceiling bookshelf installation that's a popular Instagram spot.

meals.breakfast: Insadong area — traditional Korean breakfast set at a hanok-style cafe with nurungji (scorched rice tea) and pancakes. ~₩10,000
meals.lunch: National Museum of Korea cafeteria — affordable Korean set meals with a view of the museum garden. ~₩10,000
meals.dinner: Gangnam — Hanwoo (Korean beef) Bulgogi at a mid-range Korean BBQ restaurant. ~₩25,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum is closed on Mondays (today is Tuesday — perfect timing). The Starfield Library inside COEX is free to enter and makes for a spectacular photo. Gangnam is more upscale — budget slightly more for the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Full K-culture immersion: Visit SM Town COEX Artium (K-pop themed entertainment complex) or the K-Style Hub near City Hall (free Korean Tourism Organization cultural center with K-pop, K-drama, K-food, and K-beauty exhibitions and experiences). Participate in a Hanbok dressing experience or K-pop dance intro class.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Lotte World Tower area in Jamsil. Visit the Lotte World Mall and take the elevator to the Seoul Sky observation deck on the 117th–123rd floors (~₩29,000) for the highest views in Korea. The December sky offers crystal-clear visibility on good days.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Lotte World — one of the world's largest indoor theme parks — for the evening session. December brings Christmas decorations and special winter events. Alternatively, stroll around Seokchon Lake beside Lotte World for beautiful winter reflections of the tower.

meals.breakfast: Jongno area bakery — artisan sourdough and coffee at a specialty cafe in the Ikseon-dong area. ~₩8,000
meals.lunch: Jamsil area — Jokbal (족발, braised pig's trotters) at a local restaurant near Lotte World. ~₩16,000
meals.dinner: Lotte World Mall food court or nearby Songpa-gu neighborhood — Dakgalbi (spicy stir-fried chicken) at a casual restaurant. ~₩14,000

day_by_day.notes: Seoul Sky observation deck tickets can be booked online for a discount. Evening Lotte World admission is cheaper than daytime. Seokchon Lake is free and beautifully lit at night — a great alternative to the theme park.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple (조계사) — the head temple of Korean Buddhism, located a short walk from the hotel. Admire the stunning lotus lantern decorations (often left up from November's Lantern Festival). Experience morning Buddhist rituals if timing aligns. Then explore the nearby Nakwon Arcade — a legendary multi-story musical instrument market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Ewha Womans University area in Sinchon for the afternoon. Browse the famous Ewha shopping street for affordable Korean fashion, accessories, and cosmetics. The area has a charming, youthful energy distinct from Myeongdong.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve in Seoul! Head to Myeongdong Cathedral — beautifully lit for Christmas — for the festive atmosphere. Then join the Christmas Eve celebrations in Myeongdong street or Cheonggyecheon, which will be decorated and lively. Many cafes and restaurants offer special Christmas menus.

meals.breakfast: Temple area — Vegetarian Buddhist temple food at a restaurant near Jogyesa (사찰음식). Try a simple temple cuisine set. ~₩12,000
meals.lunch: Sinchon/Ewha area — Budae Jjigae (부대찌개, Army Stew) — a Korean-American fusion stew born near US military bases, hearty and warming. ~₩13,000
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve special — splurge slightly at a traditional Korean restaurant in Myeongdong for Galbi (갈비, grilled beef short ribs) set meal. ~₩35,000

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve is one of the most festive nights in Seoul — Koreans celebrate it as a major romantic and social holiday. Book dinner reservations in advance. Myeongdong and Hongdae will be especially crowded and lively.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas morning — visit Gyeongbokgung Palace one more time for a quieter, reflective experience (many Koreans are celebrating at home). Wear a Hanbok rented from a nearby shop and enjoy the palace in winter morning light — one of the most photogenic experiences in Seoul.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the National Palace Museum of Korea (within Gyeongbokgung grounds, free entry) — a more detailed look at Joseon Dynasty royal artifacts. Then walk to Cheong Wa Dae (Blue House) for a self-guided tour of the former presidential residence, now fully open to the public.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Bukchon Hanok Village for a magical evening walk through the traditional alley (Bukchon-ro 11-gil) — the iconic view of hanok rooftops with Seoul city lights behind. Then enjoy a warm dinner in the Anguk-dong area near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Christmas morning treat — visit a specialty coffee roastery in Samcheong-dong for a pour-over coffee and croissant. ~₩10,000
meals.lunch: Palace area — Gyeongbokgung traditional snack vendors inside the palace sell Hotteok and Sikhye (sweet rice drink). Light lunch ~₩6,000
meals.dinner: Anguk-dong area — Jungsik-dang style Korean fine dining lite: try a mid-range Korean course meal restaurant for a Christmas dinner. ~₩40,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Some restaurants and shops may be closed on Christmas Day — have backup options. Bukchon Hanok Village's famous alley (Bukchon-ro 11-gil) has resident requests to be quiet after 5 PM — please be respectful.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress (수원화성) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site about 1 hour south of Seoul by subway (Line 1 to Suwon Station). Walk the full 5.7 km fortress wall circuit with stunning winter views. Visit the Hwaseong Haenggung (temporary royal palace) inside the walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Suwon's Paldalmun Gate area and the traditional market below the fortress. Return to Seoul by late afternoon. Stop at Express Bus Terminal area in Gangnam to visit the famous flower market (꽃시장) — an enormous underground flower market open late.
day_by_day.evening: Final big evening in Seoul — head to Hangang River for a night cruise (유람선). The 1-hour cruise offers spectacular views of Seoul's illuminated bridges and skyline in winter. Book at Yeouinaru or Jamsil pier (~₩15,000). Afterward, warm up with street food at a nearby pojangmacha.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area — quick Korean breakfast at a local Gimbap Cheonguk (김밥천국) chain: affordable rice rolls, soup, and fried items. ~₩7,000
meals.lunch: Suwon — Wanggalbi (왕갈비) — Suwon is famous for its giant beef short ribs. Eat at a local Suwon galbi restaurant near the fortress. ~₩25,000
meals.dinner: Han River area pojangmacha — Eomuk (fish cake) skewers, Tteokbokki, and a cup of ramyeon eaten riverside. ~₩10,000

day_by_day.notes: Check Suwon Hwaseong operating hours in advance — the fortress walls are walkable year-round but some sections may be icy in December. The Han River cruise runs year-round but schedules vary — book online in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Seoul — wake up early for one last sunrise walk around Gyeongbokgung Palace walls. Visit a nearby traditional market or neighborhood cafe for a proper Korean farewell breakfast. Pack, check out of the boutique stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time: if afternoon departure, take the AREX Express Train from Seoul Station to Incheon Airport (allow 2 hours before flight). Use any remaining time at the airport's duty-free shops for last-minute Korean beauty products, snacks (Pepero, Choco Pie, dried seaweed, instant ramyeon), and gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Incheon International Airport. Reflect on 13 incredible days of palaces, street food, K-culture, mountain hikes, and the warmth of Seoul in winter.

meals.breakfast: Final Korean breakfast — Seolleongtang (설렁탕, ox bone broth soup with rice and noodles) at a local restaurant near the hotel. ~₩12,000. A warming, nourishing farewell meal.
meals.lunch: Incheon Airport food court — have one last bowl of Korean food before departure: Bibimbap or Kimchi Jjigae. ~₩12,000
meals.dinner: In-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure at Incheon Airport. The AREX Express Train from Seoul Station takes 43 minutes. Buy any last Korean snacks and skincare at the airport duty-free — prices are competitive. Store large luggage at the hotel until checkout to keep the morning free.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Seoul, South Korea Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Incheon International Airport at 13:00 — skip morning activities. Private luxury transfer arranged via limousine service (KAL Limousine or premium chauffeur) to boutique hotel in Gyeongbokgung, Jongno-gu. Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your accommodations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation stroll through Bukchon Hanok Village, just minutes from the hotel. Wander the traditional alleyways of preserved Joseon-era hanok homes, absorbing the atmosphere of old Seoul against the backdrop of Gyeongbokgung Palace walls. Stop at a traditional tea house for a warm welcome cup of yujacha (citron tea) or omija tea.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Gaon (3 Michelin stars, Sinsa-dong) — one of Seoul's most celebrated fine dining institutions specializing in royal Korean court cuisine. Elegant multi-course hansik tasting menu featuring seasonal ingredients. After dinner, return to the hotel and enjoy a nightcap at a nearby rooftop bar with views of Gyeongbokgung's illuminated palace walls.

meals.breakfast: On the flight or at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Light snack or airport lounge dining upon arrival — alternatively, a quick premium bowl of seolleongtang (ox bone soup) near the hotel to warm up after travel
meals.dinner: Gaon Restaurant — royal Korean court cuisine tasting menu (approx. KRW 250,000–350,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Jet lag may be a factor — keep Day 1 light. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance. December in Seoul is cold (average -2°C to 5°C), so pack thermal layers, a heavy coat, gloves, and a scarf. The boutique hotel's concierge can assist with restaurant reservations and local tips.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Gyeongbokgung Palace, the grandest of Seoul's Five Grand Palaces, right at your doorstep. Witness the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony (10:00 and 14:00 daily). Explore the National Folk Museum of Korea located within the palace grounds for an immersive introduction to Korean heritage and customs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Cheong Wa Dae (Blue House) — the former presidential residence opened to the public in 2022, offering stunning architecture and gardens. Afterward, explore Samcheong-dong, a charming neighborhood of art galleries, boutique shops, and cafés. Browse the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art (MMCA) Seoul branch for cutting-edge Korean contemporary art.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Mingles (2 Michelin stars, Cheongdam-dong) — Chef Kang Min-goo's celebrated restaurant blending Korean flavors with global techniques. Creative seasonal tasting menu. Post-dinner, explore the atmospheric lantern-lit streets near Insadong for a evening walk through Korea's cultural arts district.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast or visit Café Bora (Insadong) for premium matcha and traditional Korean pastries
meals.lunch: Bukchon Son Mandu — artisanal handmade dumplings in a hanok setting near Gyeongbokgung
meals.dinner: Mingles — modern Korean tasting menu (approx. KRW 200,000–280,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung Palace opens at 09:00. Wear comfortable walking shoes — the palace grounds are expansive. Hanbok rental is available at the palace entrance for a premium photo experience and free entry in traditional dress. Book Mingles well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace and its UNESCO-listed Secret Garden (Huwon). The Secret Garden tour must be booked in advance and is limited to small groups — an exclusive experience through centuries-old pavilions, ponds, and forested walking paths. In winter, the bare trees and frost-dusted ground create a serene, painterly atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Insadong in depth — Seoul's premier cultural shopping street. Visit Ssamziegil, an innovative courtyard mall featuring independent Korean designers, artisans, and craft studios. Purchase premium Korean souvenirs: hand-painted fans, celadon pottery, hanji paper crafts, and traditional tea sets. Stop at the Korea Furniture Museum (by appointment only) for a rare look at exquisite Joseon-era wooden furniture in a hanok compound.
day_by_day.evening: Private traditional Korean cooking class with a master chef — learn to prepare royal court banchan (side dishes), japchae, and a signature Korean dish. Enjoy your creations as dinner in an intimate hanok setting. Alternatively, dine at Jungsik Seoul (2 Michelin stars) for avant-garde Korean cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Tosokchon Samgyetang — legendary ginseng chicken soup restaurant near Gyeongbokgung, a Seoul institution
meals.lunch: Balwoo Gongyang — temple food restaurant at Jogyesa Temple, a meditative and exquisite vegetarian Korean meal
meals.dinner: Private cooking class dinner or Jungsik Seoul tasting menu (approx. KRW 220,000–300,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Changdeokgung Secret Garden tours are ticketed and timed — book online at least 2–3 weeks in advance. The Korea Furniture Museum requires advance reservations and is a hidden gem beloved by design enthusiasts. Jogyesa Temple is the head temple of Korean Buddhism and worth a brief visit before or after lunch.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the UNESCO World Heritage site of Hwaseong Fortress in Suwon (approx. 1 hour by KTX or private car). Walk the 5.7km fortress walls encircling the city — a masterpiece of 18th-century military architecture. Visit Hwaseong Haenggung (temporary palace) and explore the traditional market town below the fortress.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Seoul and head to Itaewon and the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art — one of Asia's finest private art museums, housing an extraordinary collection of Korean antiquities alongside international contemporary art by Damien Hirst, Jeff Koons, and others. The building itself, designed by three world-renowned architects (Mario Botta, Jean Nouvel, Rem Koolhaas), is an architectural marvel.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at La Yeon (3 Michelin stars, The Shilla Hotel) — the pinnacle of Korean fine dining with panoramic views of Seoul. Chef's tasting menu featuring the finest seasonal Korean ingredients prepared with extraordinary refinement. After dinner, evening cocktails at the hotel bar with views of Namsan Tower.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Suwon Wanggalbi — famous premium galbi (short ribs) near Hwaseong Fortress, a local specialty
meals.dinner: La Yeon at The Shilla Hotel — 3 Michelin star Korean tasting menu (approx. KRW 300,000–400,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: A private car with driver is recommended for the Suwon day trip for maximum comfort and flexibility. La Yeon is one of the hardest reservations to secure in Seoul — book months in advance. Dress code at La Yeon is smart formal.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Namdaemun Market and Myeongdong — Seoul's bustling commercial heart. Visit Namdaemun for premium Korean street food: hotteok (sweet pancakes), tteokbokki, and freshly grilled seafood. Then head to Myeongdong for luxury K-beauty shopping at flagship stores of Sulwhasoo, History of Whoo, and O HUI — Korea's most prestigious skincare brands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cable car ride up to N Seoul Tower (Namsan Tower) for panoramic 360-degree views of the city skyline. Visit the tower's observation deck and add a love lock to the famous fence. Afterward, explore the charming Namsangol Hanok Village at the base of Namsan mountain — a reconstructed traditional village with cultural performances.
day_by_day.evening: Experience a traditional Korean performance at the National Theater of Korea on Namsan — check December schedule for gugak (traditional music), pansori, or a special winter performance. Pre-show dinner at Hanilkwan — one of Seoul's oldest and most respected traditional Korean restaurants, beloved for its galbi and royal court dishes.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Namdaemun Market premium street food crawl — hotteok, gimbap, grilled shellfish, and bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes)
meals.dinner: Hanilkwan — classic Korean fine dining institution (approx. KRW 80,000–150,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Myeongdong on Saturdays can be very crowded — go early. Sulwhasoo's flagship store offers personalized skincare consultations and premium gift packaging. Check the National Theater of Korea's December program online and book tickets in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private calligraphy and hanji (Korean paper) art workshop with a master artist in a traditional Jongno studio. Learn the meditative art of Korean brush calligraphy and create your own piece to take home as a unique souvenir. Explore Gyeonghuigung Palace — the least visited of Seoul's Five Grand Palaces, offering a peaceful and intimate experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan — one of the world's largest museums, housing over 220,000 artifacts spanning Korean history from prehistoric times through the Joseon Dynasty. The collection of gold crowns, celadon pottery, and Buddhist art is world-class. Enjoy the museum's serene reflecting pool (frozen beautifully in December).
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Kwon Sook-soo — an intimate, reservation-only Korean fine dining experience in a converted hanok in Jongno. Chef Kwon's deeply personal interpretation of Korean cuisine using heirloom ingredients is a transcendent experience. Post-dinner, a curated whisky tasting at Charles H. (Four Seasons Hotel Seoul) — Seoul's most celebrated cocktail bar.

meals.breakfast: Café Onion Anguk — a beautifully designed café in a restored hanok near Gyeongbokgung, famous for premium pastries and coffee
meals.lunch: Museum restaurant or nearby Yongsan premium Korean BBQ at Maple Tree House
meals.dinner: Kwon Sook-soo — intimate Korean fine dining (approx. KRW 250,000–350,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Kwon Sook-soo is extremely exclusive with very limited seating — reservations must be made months ahead. The National Museum of Korea is free entry. Charles H. at Four Seasons Seoul is a world-class cocktail experience — reservations recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Immersive K-pop cultural experience: Visit HYBE Insight, the official museum of HYBE Entertainment (BTS, TXT, NewJeans) in Yongsan. Interactive exhibits explore the creative process behind K-pop from music production to choreography, fashion, and global cultural impact. Book premium tickets well in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Gangnam district — Seoul's most affluent neighborhood. Visit the COEX Mall and its spectacular Starfield Library (a stunning public library within the mall). Browse Apgujeong Rodeo Street for luxury Korean and international fashion boutiques. Visit the flagship stores of high-end Korean designers like Wooyoungmi and Juun.J.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Sushi Saito Seoul (if available) or Atomix (2 Michelin stars, Midtown) — Chef Park Junghyun's extraordinary 10-course Korean tasting menu blending culinary artistry with cultural storytelling through beautifully illustrated menu cards. One of the most acclaimed dining experiences in Asia.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Bonchon — premium Korean fried chicken in Gangnam, or a refined bibimbap set at a high-end Korean restaurant in COEX
meals.dinner: Atomix — 10-course Korean tasting menu (approx. KRW 350,000–450,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: HYBE Insight tickets sell out weeks in advance — book immediately upon confirming your trip. Atomix is consistently ranked among the World's 50 Best Restaurants — reservations are extremely competitive and open 60 days in advance. Smart casual dress recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nami Island (Namiseom) — a scenic crescent-shaped river island famous for its tree-lined avenues and romantic atmosphere, made iconic by the K-drama Winter Sonata. In December, the island is dusted with frost and decorated for winter, creating a magical atmosphere. Take the ferry from Gapyeong. Optional zip-line over the river for a thrill.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Petite France — a whimsical French-themed cultural village in Gapyeong, featured in the K-drama My Love from the Star. Explore the colorful buildings, Le Petit Prince exhibitions, and cultural performances. Return to Seoul by private car or ITX train in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Congdu — a sophisticated Korean-Chinese fusion restaurant in a beautifully restored hanok in Jongno, known for its elegant atmosphere and creative menu. After dinner, explore the atmospheric Gwanghwamun Square illuminated with winter lights and seasonal decorations.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or pick up premium kimbap and coffee for the journey
meals.lunch: Nami Island's Naminara Restaurant or a packed premium picnic lunch arranged by the hotel's concierge
meals.dinner: Congdu — Korean-Chinese fusion in a hanok setting (approx. KRW 100,000–180,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: A private car with driver is strongly recommended for the Nami Island day trip for maximum flexibility and comfort in winter. The drive is approximately 1.5 hours each way. Dress in extra warm layers — Nami Island is exposed and very cold in December. The island is magical in winter with minimal crowds compared to autumn.

day_by_day.morning: Traditional Korean wellness morning: Begin with a private session at a premium jjimjilbang (Korean bathhouse) — opt for the luxurious Dragon Hill Spa or a private suite at a high-end spa hotel. Experience the full ritual of hot and cold baths, body scrub (Italy towel exfoliation), and infrared sauna. A deeply restorative Korean cultural tradition.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — Zaha Hadid's iconic futuristic building, a marvel of parametric architecture. Visit the design exhibitions and pop-up shows inside. Browse the adjacent Dongdaemun Market for premium Korean textiles and fashion. Visit the Seoul Museum of History nearby for a curated look at Seoul's transformation over the centuries.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Korean tea ceremony experience at a premium tea house in Insadong or Bukchon — a meditative and culturally rich ritual. Dinner at Ryunique (1 Michelin star) — Chef Ryu Tae-hwan's innovative Korean-French cuisine in an intimate setting in Gangnam.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the spa or hotel
meals.lunch: Gwangjang Market — Seoul's oldest covered market, famous for premium bindaetteok, mayak gimbap, and yukhoe (Korean beef tartare). A legendary food experience.
meals.dinner: Ryunique — Korean-French tasting menu (approx. KRW 180,000–250,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the private spa suite in advance for a truly luxurious experience. Gwangjang Market is a must-visit culinary landmark — the yukhoe (raw beef) stalls are particularly famous. DDP hosts rotating design exhibitions — check the December schedule for special winter shows.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple — the spiritual heart of Korean Buddhism in central Seoul, beautifully decorated with thousands of lanterns for the winter season. Experience a morning meditation session with monks (advance booking required). Explore the temple's serene grounds and the Buddhist Cultural Center adjacent to it.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private K-drama and K-culture filming locations tour — visit iconic locations from beloved dramas set in Jongno, Bukchon, and Mapo. A private guide with deep knowledge of Korean pop culture will bring the dramas to life. Stop at the Korean Wave (Hallyu) cultural experience center for an immersive look at how K-pop, K-drama, and K-beauty conquered the world.
day_by_day.evening: Special Christmas Eve dinner at The Dining Room at Park Hyatt Seoul — an elegant Western-Korean fusion holiday dinner with panoramic night views of Seoul. The city comes alive with Christmas lights and decorations. After dinner, stroll through the beautifully illuminated streets of Cheonggyecheon Stream, where the annual lantern festival creates a magical winter wonderland.

meals.breakfast: Temple vegetarian breakfast (if available through the meditation program) or hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Noryangjin Fish Market — visit the famous wholesale fish market and have your premium selection (king crab, abalone, sea urchin) cooked to order upstairs
meals.dinner: The Dining Room, Park Hyatt Seoul — Christmas Eve special menu (approx. KRW 200,000–300,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas is widely celebrated in Seoul with spectacular light displays throughout the city. Cheonggyecheon Stream's lantern installations are particularly beautiful on Christmas Eve. Book the Christmas Eve dinner well in advance as it sells out quickly. Noryangjin Fish Market is open early morning — a lunch visit works well.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise hike up Bugaksan Mountain — the mountain directly behind Gyeongbokgung Palace, offering spectacular panoramic views of Seoul at dawn. A moderately easy hike with a premium reward: watching the winter sun rise over the Han River and city skyline. Return to the hotel for a leisurely Christmas morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Whanki Museum — a beautiful private museum dedicated to Korean abstract expressionist Kim Whanki, set in a stunning building in Buam-dong, a tranquil hillside neighborhood. Explore the charming Buam-dong café district — Seoul's most artistically curated neighborhood with independent galleries, bookshops, and design studios hidden among quiet residential alleys.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Day private dining experience — arrange through the hotel concierge for an exclusive in-room or private dining room experience featuring a curated Korean holiday menu, or reserve a table at Dani's (1 Michelin star) for an intimate Christmas dinner. End the evening with premium champagne and desserts at the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Special hotel Christmas breakfast — arrange in advance with the hotel for a festive spread
meals.lunch: Buam-dong café lunch — try Sanmotoonge, a legendary café with stunning city views and homemade Korean desserts
meals.dinner: Private in-room dining or Dani's restaurant — Christmas tasting menu (approx. KRW 200,000–300,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Bugaksan requires registration at the checkpoint — bring your passport. The hike takes approximately 1.5–2 hours round trip. Dress in full winter gear. Buam-dong is best explored on foot and is one of Seoul's most photogenic and peaceful neighborhoods — a welcome contrast to the city's energy.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day premium experience: Private kimchi-making and Korean fermentation masterclass with a renowned kimchi artisan. Learn the ancient art of kimchi preparation, including traditional onggi (clay pot) fermentation methods, and create your own batch to take home vacuum-sealed. Explore the Korean Kimchi Cultural Center for deeper context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bukchon area's premium antique and art galleries — Gana Art Gallery and Arario Gallery Seoul are excellent choices for high-end Korean contemporary and traditional art. Consider purchasing a piece of Korean art as a lasting memento. Visit the newly opened Seoul Museum of Craft Art for an exquisite showcase of Korean craft traditions from pottery to metalwork.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell pre-departure dinner at Soil — an intimate, reservation-only restaurant in Seongbuk-dong where Chef Yim Jungsik (different from Jungsik restaurant) serves a deeply personal Korean tasting menu rooted in seasonal and fermented ingredients. Alternatively, a premium Korean BBQ experience at Maple Tree House Hannam — premium Hanwoo beef (Korean wagyu) grilled tableside with an extensive banchan spread.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Light lunch during the kimchi masterclass — traditional Korean table set with freshly made kimchi, rice, and doenjang jjigae (fermented soybean paste stew)
meals.dinner: Maple Tree House Hannam — premium Hanwoo Korean BBQ (approx. KRW 150,000–250,000 per person) or fine dining alternative

day_by_day.notes: Book the kimchi masterclass well in advance — private sessions with master artisans are limited. Vacuum-sealed kimchi can be packed in checked luggage. Gana Art Gallery is one of Korea's most prestigious galleries with English-speaking staff. This is the last full evening — take time to reflect on the journey.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Seoul — leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Last stroll through the Gyeongbokgung neighborhood and Bukchon Hanok Village to soak in the atmosphere one final time. Visit a premium tea shop in Insadong to purchase high-quality Korean teas (nokcha, boricha, omija) as gifts. Pick up any last-minute souvenirs at Ssamziegil or local artisan shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out from the hotel. Private luxury limousine transfer to Incheon International Airport. Arrive at the airport with ample time — enjoy the airport's premium lounges (Korean Air Prestige Lounge or Asiana Club Lounge are world-class). Browse Incheon's extensive duty-free shopping for Korean beauty, spirits, and luxury goods.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Incheon International Airport. Carry the memories of 13 extraordinary days immersed in the culture, cuisine, history, and contemporary brilliance of Seoul.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — request a special farewell spread from the hotel
meals.lunch: Premium airport dining at Incheon — try the Korean restaurant in the departure terminal for a final bowl of doenjang jjigae or galbitang (short rib soup)
meals.dinner: In-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3–3.5 hours before departure for check-in, immigration, and airport exploration at Incheon — consistently rated the world's best airport. Incheon's duty-free offers some of the best prices globally on K-beauty, Korean ginseng products, and premium spirits. Confirm private transfer booking the evening before. Keep all receipts for VAT refund at the airport — significant savings on luxury purchases.

query: Seoul K-culture and food, $2200 couple, winter 2026 from LAX
